title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: The National Confederation of Employers of Moldova (CNPM) is the main employer representative in the country. While its membership is stable, it continues to be relatively low, partly due to limited awareness among companies of the benefits of collective action. The government's increasing reliance on direct consultations with competing business associations and chambers - through alternative platforms rather than traditional tripartite social dialogue - has further fragmented employer representation. This shift has weakened the CNPM’s position by reducing its influence in key policy discussions and indirectly constraining its growth. To strengthen its role, the CNPM must enhance its policy engagement and diversify its service portfolio to better reach underrepresented business segments, including women entrepreneurs. Promoting measures that support formalisation would also expand its potential membership base. To support these goals, in 2024-2025 the ILO is assisting the CNPM in developing evidence-based recommendations to support its advocacy efforts for the advancement of women in business and management. The CNPM will also be supported in establishing a new service to help companies design comprehensive workplace policies aimed at attracting, retaining, and advancing women - particularly into managerial positions - in alignment with international labour standards, national legislation, and best practices. The ILO will continue to assist the CNPM’s advocacy efforts in the area of formalisation. A sub-regional policy forum will be organised to build the CNPM’s capacity to promote incentive-based formalisation strategies. In parallel, the CNPM will receive support in conducting awareness raising campaigns on formalisation in the agricultural sector, complementing efforts by the Ministry of Labour by encouraging agricultural businesses to utilise the newly introduced voucher system.
